name: Transitional Housing Program
description:
The transitional housing programs available for families experiencing homelessness, assist them in developing and strengthening skills to acquire and maintain permanent housing. 

Helping with barriers such as:
- Behavioral health therapy
- Substance use 
- Domestic violence
- Immigration
- Life skills building

Transitional Housing offers private living accommodations and comprehensive support services for 20 families for up to 12 months. 
- Employment 
- Education
- Financial literacy
- Parenting education
application_process:
Visit a coordinated entry access point. Go here for more information
https://www.sf.gov/resource--2024--get-person-homelessness-help-san-francisco

Then, at the Access Point, a “Housing Problem Solving Specialist”  will talk with you about your family’s situation and find the best option available. If you qualify, you can receive referrals to programs providing rental subsidies, transitional housing, or permanent supportive housing.

Go here for more:
https://hamiltonfamilies.org/get-help

name: Supportive Housing
description:
Conard House operates and provides social services at 10 residential hotels and 22 private apartments scattered across San Francisco. All Supportive Housing residents have access to a compassionate community of: 
- Therapists
- Case Managers/Social Workers
- Health Navigators
- Financial Budget Counselors
- Digital Educators
- Job Counselors
- 24-Hour Desk Clerks
- Property Managers
- Administrators

These Supportive Housing (SH) communities provide homes for 730 people with mental health conditions. Often times, such conditions are exacerbated by chronic medical ailments and/or substance use. One of the SH sites offers a 2 year transitional program as a bridge often from residential treatment to independent living. Residents would be homeless or at risk of being homeless without the daily resources Conard House provides. These resources extend over and above affordable housing.

For Housing referral information for the **Aranda, Allen, McAllister, Lyric and Plaza**, please contact the Adult Coordinated Entry Access Points. Access Points provide problem solving, assessment, prioritization, and referral to housing and other community services for San Francisco adults experiencing homelessness.

Adults over the age of 18 without minor children who are experiencing or at risk of homelessness can call (415) 487-3300 extension 7000 to reach the following Access Points:

name: Anti-Trafficking Program
description:
The Anti-Trafficking Program provides comprehensive, survivor-centered support for individuals who have experienced labor or sex trafficking. Services are designed to help survivors achieve safety, stability, and long-term independence through culturally responsive and trauma-informed care.

Support may include individualized case management, safety planning, emergency assistance, advocacy, referrals to medical and mental health services, immigration support, housing resources, legal referrals, and connections to community services. Asian Women's Shelter provides services in 41 languages to ensure survivors can access assistance in a linguistically and culturally appropriate environment.

The service provides trafficked people with the following legal and social services:
- Legal Assistance
- Assistance with VISA
- Shelter
- Case management
- Interpretation
- Advocacy
- Independent living skills

description:

name: CalWORKs
description:
SFHSA has the California Work Opportunity and Responsibility to Kids (CalWORKs) program to provide eligible families and expectant mothers with a variety of temporary services, including the following:

- Cash assistance (Financial support, Diversion, and Immigrant support)
- Child care and parenting (including free diapers)
- Employment and education (including job assistance)
- Food and health (CalFresh, CalMedi, and counseling)
- Housing assistance (including eviction prevention)
- Transportation allowance
- Other free or steeply discounted services

- In person at 170 Otis Street Service Center

Schedule and complete CalWORKS appointment

name: Compass Clara House
description:
Compass Clara House is an 6–18 month transitional housing program where families live in private apartments and receive intensive wrap-around support. 

Services:
- Housing in 13 individual family apartments within a uniquely supportive community
- 6 to 18-month action plans designed with each family to help clients achieve their education, career and housing goals
- Intensive case management
- Hands-on employment, education, and life skills support for parents
- Full-day licensed childcare for children through age five, and an afterschool homework and tutoring program for older children and teenagers
- Housing search assistance for families graduating from the program
- Follow-up after-care support provided for one year

Compass Clara House/Helen Hawk Children’s Center participates in the California Child & Adult Food Program (CACFP).
